msdyn_plan.msdyn_description: This app empowers schedulers, supervisors, and employees to plan, visualize, and manage production jobs easily for efficient sign manufacturing.
msdyn_plan.msdyn_prompt:
Build a canvas app for production scheduling connected to Microsoft Business Central data where possible, but do not require custom APIs or admin-only changes.
Goal: Create a scheduling app for a sign manufacturing company that helps schedule jobs, departments, resources, and employees based on estimated labor hours.
Main requirements: 1. Create a dashboard with department tiles: - All Active Production Work - Metal Fab - Paint - Vinyl / Graphics - Assembly - Routing - Install / Loading - QC / Ready to Ship - Overloaded / At Risk
Each tile should show job count, total estimated hours, scheduled hours, unscheduled hours, and capacity remaining.
2. Create a Job Search screen: - Search by Job No. - Show job name, customer, due date, department/resource, estimated labor hours, planning line reference, and status. - Allow imported or manually entered estimate/resource lines if Business Central connector access is limited.
3. Create an Employee Setup screen: Track employee name, department, normal work days, start time, end time, lunch start, lunch duration, daily capacity hours, and optional overtime hours.
Example: Monday–Friday, 7:00 AM–3:30 PM, 30-minute lunch at 12:00 PM.
4. Create a Scheduling screen: Allow the user to select: - Job No. - Department/resource line - Employee - Estimated labor hours - Required completion date/time - Optional overtime hours
The app should calculate a realistic start date/time by back-scheduling from the completion date based on the employee’s available working hours.
If estimated hours exceed one day, split the work across multiple workdays instead of scheduling after hours.
5. Create schedule blocks: Each scheduled block should include: - Job No. - Department - Employee - Start DateTime - End DateTime - Scheduled Hours - Completion DateTime - Overtime Used - Notes
6. Add conflict detection: Flag overlapping work for the same employee where: Existing StartDateTime < New EndDateTime and Existing EndDateTime > New StartDateTime
Show conflicts in red and create an “Overloaded / At Risk” view.
7. Create a weekly calendar view: - Rows = employees - Columns = Monday through Saturday - Show scheduled job cards inside each employee/day cell - Allow filtering by department - Include unscheduled work queue on the right side
8. Store scheduling data in a SharePoint list or Dataverse for Teams table called Production Schedule Lines. Use Business Central as the source for job/estimate information where the connector allows, but keep scheduling assignments in the app database.
9. Include a Review & Commit screen: Before finalizing schedules, show all schedule blocks, conflicts, unscheduled hours, and overloaded employees. Allow export/print so the schedule can be manually updated in Business Central if write-back permissions are not available.
10. Use a clean modern layout with dark navy primary color #141464, red accent #E8151B, white cards, rounded corners, and clear department status colors.
Build the app with the following tables: - Employees - Departments - Job Estimate Lines - Production Schedule Lines - Employee Work Hours - Overtime Overrides
Make the app beginner-friendly, with clear screens, simple forms, editable galleries, and formulas that can be expanded later.
